newsitem.title: USA: AMERICAN FOOTBALL-PANTHERS BEAT COWBOYS TO MOVE ONE GAME FROM THE SUPER BOWL.
newsitem.headline: AMERICAN FOOTBALL-PANTHERS BEAT COWBOYS TO MOVE ONE GAME FROM THE SUPER BOWL.

text.p: The two-year-old Carolina Panthers intercepted Troy Aikman three times and muzzled Emmit Smith to beat defending Super Bowl champions Dallas Cowboys 26-17 in an NFC divisional playoff on Sunday.

Panthers' quarterback Kerry Collins, who grew up idolising Aikman, threw two touchdown pases, and John Kasay kicked four field goals to take the Panthers to next Sunday's National Football Conference title game against the Green Bay Packers. The winner will go to the Super Bowl on January 26.
Collins completed 12-of-22 passes for 100 yards. Willie Green caught five passes for 53 yards and a score.

Carolina outplayed Dallas in every phase of the game, particularly on defence. The Panthers picked off Troy Aikman three times and limited Emmitt Smith to 80 yards -- and no touchdowns -- on 22 carries.
"We are the new kids on the block," said Panthers' corner back Eric Davis. "To get to the Super Bowl we have stopped San Francisco and now we beat the Man, the champion Dallas Cowboys."

Anthony Johnson rushed for 104 yards for the Panthers (13-4), who knocked stars Michael Irvin and Deion Sanders out of the game with injuries and kept the rest of the Cowboys from scoring in the second half.

Playing their first playoff game, the Panthers were not intimidated by the Cowboys (11-7), who had won three of the last four Super Bowls. But this season it seemed the Cowboys were affected by a stream of distractions, suspensions and injuries.

The latest Cowboys' problem was the recent naming by a 23-year-old woman of Irvin and offensive tackle Erik Williams in a sexual assault complaint. Irvin did not return to the game after injuring his shoulder in the first quarter.

"That's all it takes," said Dallas lineman Nate Newton. "When anyone male, female, animal, child, anything or anybody can make a claim against the Dallas Cowboys it has to have an effect. You can't prepare for a game like this with something like that going on. You can't focus, you are worrying about other things."
Even the special teams, which cost Carolina five points earlier in the game, played a key role.

After Chris Boniol's 21-yard field goal goal pulled Dallas within 23-17 with 5:33 remaining, Michael Bates returned the ensuing kickoff 51 yards. Carolina went three-and-out, but Rohn Stark's punt was downed by Johnson at the Cowboys 1.

With the help of two penalties, Aikman drove Dallas to the 32 before his long pass up the right sideline was intercepted by Pat Terrell, who returned it 49 yards to the Cowboys 19. Kasay kicked a 32-yarder and linebacker Sam Mills added an interception to seal the victory.

Collins stayed away from Sanders, preferring to go after Kevin Smith instead. Sanders was injured on offence, when his head was driven to the turf after a 16-yard run on a reverse that set up Boniol's last field goal.
Aikman was 18-of-36 for 165 yards and a touchdown and was sacked twice. Kevin Williams caught six passes for 89 yards.
After throwing an early interception, Collins had a pair of TD passes less than eight minutes apart in the first half and the Panthers never trailed again.
